stem: What characterizes the 'tangential excision' technique developed by Zora Janovich?

options.text: The removal of the entire skin layer down to the muscle fascia.
The use of a high-pressure saline jet to selectively dissolve dead tissue.
Removing thin slivers of eschar sequentially until a viable, bleeding base is reached.
Excision of a circular area of skin including a wide margin of healthy tissue.

explanation: Tangential excision aims to minimize the loss of healthy tissue by shaving away only the dead layers (eschar).
rationale: Think about how a surgeon might minimize tissue loss by working in layers.

optionExplanations.A: This describes a more radical excision used in the past, whereas tangential excision is more conservative.
optionExplanations.B: This describes the Versajet system, which is a modern alternative but not the Janovich technique itself.
optionExplanations.C: Tangential excision aims to minimize the loss of healthy tissue by shaving away only the dead layers (eschar).
optionExplanations.D: This technique is more common in oncology than in burn management where tissue preservation is critical.
